title: Push demand harder

predict.q: The economy starts with spare capacity: output 480, full-employment output 500. AD rises by 40 in total. What happens?

options.s: Real output rises by the full 40, to 520; the price level does not change
options.fb: Output can rise by the full amount only with lots of spare capacity and flat AS. Near capacity, prices rise instead.

options.s: The price level rises a lot; real output stays at 480
options.fb: There is spare capacity at first (output 480 < 500), so output does rise.

options.s: Real output rises a lot; unemployment and inflation both fall
options.fb: More demand lowers unemployment but raises inflation: the two move in opposite directions here.

options.s: Real output rises by less than 40; the price level rises a lot
options.fb: Output 480 → 503 (+8, +7, +5, +3) while the price level climbs 100 → 117 (+2, +3, +5, +7).

task: Move the AD slider up in steps of 10 and watch output, the price level, unemployment and imports.

target.do: Move the AD slider up to 40, then press Check.

takeaway: Each extra push buys less output and more inflation as the economy nears capacity.
